newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Viasa holders want job cuts, to meet Sat on future.
newsitem.headline: Viasa holders want job cuts, to meet Sat on future.

text.p: Shareholders in Venezuelan airline Viasa have asked for cuts of over 300 jobs as part of a wider restructuring plan just ahead of a critical meeting Saturday to decide whether or not to seek bankruptcy, workers said.

Workers, however, said they have yet to receive the plan. Iberia Lineas Aereas de Espana and the Venezuela Investment Fund (FIV) will only inject $25 million to refloat the troubled company if the plan is approved. The FIV is Venezuela's privatization agency.
"They've asked us to reduce personnel by 346 jobs," said workers representative William Bracho. "But we're still waiting for copies of the plan they promised us."
The FIV, which owns 40 percent of Viasa, and Iberia, which owns 45 percent, hammered out the restructuring agreement in talks late January after Viasa suspended all flights on January 23.

The grounding came after workers rejected a previous cost- cutting proposal by Iberia that included 20 percent job reductions, a wage freeze and dropping unprofitable routes. Viasa employs 2,200 ground and air staff.

If the latest proposal is cleared on Saturday, the FIV has said Iberia will probably retire from managing the airline. It is also now looking for a new investor willing to run and recapitalize the company.
